claims.statement: The admitted teaching DAG has concrete parent-existence/generation checks and graph traversal. All64 four-vertex forward-edge DAGs pass512 independent ancestor/descendant comparisons. This supports bounded reachability behavior, not authenticity of the declared causal graph.

The small inverse-lineage rank example agrees with an exact two-node stationary equation under uniform dangling redistribution. Mixed-direction Pareto comparisons also correctly exclude a strictly dominated distinct-ID control. These are mathematical toy mechanisms; they establish no model improvement.

The EIS fixture gate actually calls a supplied detector on retained positive/negative examples and rejects an empty polarity side; the byte filter, substring match and caller-count policies are explicit finite computations. They offer useful baseline components when their evidence and authority limits are preserved.

findings.statement: LamarckianEngine prescribes better correctness and latency without evaluating the changed prompt; an empty reflection keeps the exact genotype but still moves score0.5 to0.55 and latency10 to9.5. Its retained test asserts this manufactured improvement. These fields cannot be used as empirical workflow outcomes.
findings.recommended_action: Keep synthetic dynamics explicitly separated from measured results; require an independent held-out evaluation and actual usage/time receipts for benchmark comparisons.

findings.statement: The toy forge can change the task itself, with no protected-span input or semantic-preservation witness. A public J=1 to J=2 mutation is accepted. Token edits and appended reflection text are not an implementation of the protected-core contract.
findings.recommended_action: Bind immutable task material and a scoped preservation check before exposing these mutation operators to the shared-seed benchmark.

findings.statement: The EIS toy ExternalAdmissionBoundary returns admitted=True after byte/substring screening and never consults its supplied thymus or an external decision. TwoSignalGuard trusts its Boolean input, and SupportPolicy accepts empty support when configured with zero. These are toy filtering/counting policies, not authenticated admission or independent-evidence enforcement.
findings.recommended_action: Use screening-specific result names and explicit admitted-parameter/witness boundaries; keep this simulation separate from actual authorization.

findings.statement: The standalone Pareto list selector skips comparisons for equal IDs, so a strictly dominated duplicate-ID member remains on the returned frontier. A distinct-ID control is correctly removed.
findings.recommended_action: Validate unique candidate identity before selection or compare the intended occurrence identity explicitly.

findings.statement: Taint is a snapshot set, and later children stay unquarantined until an explicit rescan. Island migration does not consult that set or enforce its stored capacity; a quarantined source moves into a full capacity-one target, leaving two members. No integrated fail-closed quarantine/capacity workflow follows from these classes.
findings.recommended_action: Declare update-time taint and admission checks and enforce target capacity before state changes if these demos are adapted into workflows.

findings.statement: The event-log verifier accepts a truncated prefix while last_hash still names the removed tail. It verifies only surviving links/data, not the retained head, expected length, durable storage or an external anchor. Ordinary payload tampering is detected.
findings.recommended_action: Check the bound expected head and sequence/length, and distinguish local chain consistency from durable authenticated append-only history.
